title: Knowledge check: Automatic Values and Generated Identifiers

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies to “Automatic Values and Generated Identifiers”?
options: Rely on undocumented behavior and skip checking the actual SQLite runtime.
Concatenate untrusted input directly into SQL and suppress errors.
Assume the result is correct without checking the schema, data or expected output.
Check the SQLite runtime is at least 3.35.0 and handle the returned rows in the application API.
questions.answer_key: Check the SQLite runtime is at least 3.35.0 and handle the returned rows in the application API.
questions.explanation: Automatic Values and Generated Identifiers: Check the SQLite runtime is at least 3.35.0 and handle the returned rows in the application API. RETURNING is available from SQLite 3.35.0; embedded runtimes may lag behind the shell installed on a computer.

questions.prompt: When a minimal example for “Automatic Values and Generated Identifiers” behaves unexpectedly, what is the best next step?
options: Reduce it to a reproducible fixture, inspect schema and values, and verify the expected result.
Change several unrelated statements at once and rerun against important production data.
Ignore the runtime version and assume every SQLite build includes every optional feature.
Disable constraints so the current test always passes.
questions.answer_key: Reduce it to a reproducible fixture, inspect schema and values, and verify the expected result.
questions.explanation: A controlled fixture helps isolate behavior and makes the test repeatable. Preserve constraints and state the assumptions you verified.

questions.prompt: What should be recorded before depending on an SQLite capability related to “Automatic Values and Generated Identifiers”?
options: The installed CLI only; the linked library and build options never differ.
The library version linked into the application, relevant feature/build support, and a small compatibility test.
Nothing, because SQLite automatically upgrades the application runtime.
questions.answer_key: The library version linked into the application, relevant feature/build support, and a small compatibility test.
questions.explanation: The CLI and application may be linked to different SQLite versions, and some capabilities depend on compile-time options or loaded extensions.
